=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible paired leaves attached at the same node along the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are crowded at the apex of the seedling stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided laminae)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are linear-lanceolate to lanceolate in shape, widest below the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (apex tapers gradually to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (base tapers to a narrow wedge-like shape at the petiole attachment)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, relatively close spacing, numerous (clearly visible arching towards the margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (upper surface reflects light, indicating a smooth, waxy texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth and glabrous)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are clearly visible but relatively short compared to the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears green, slender, and non-woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears smooth and glabrous)
    19. Stem color: green with reddish tinge (main stem is green, with a noticeable reddish hue at the nodes and younger growth)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem surface appears even without obvious ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): unclear (axillary regions are crowded, making definitive identification of stipules difficult)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint-like structure visible at the petiole base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Damage is present on some leaves, including white surface markings (likely dried sap or residue) and small holes. The seedling has a tag labeled "SPAGU 5" attached to the stem.
